## Purpose and scope

This policy explains normal international delivery timing and customer responsibility for import charges. It applies only to countries shown as eligible at checkout.

## Standard rule

International orders normally arrive in 7 to 14 business days after shipment. Import duties, taxes, and customs fees are the customer responsibility unless checkout explicitly states that duties are prepaid. Customs processing can add time outside BrightCart control.

## Conditions and decision points

- The destination country must be supported at checkout.
- Carrier tracking may pause while a package is in customs.
- The customer is responsible for accurate recipient and tax information.

A package ships from the United States to France and reaches customs after six business days. The carrier requests a local import tax before final delivery. The customer pays that fee because the order was not marked duties prepaid.

- Some promotions include duties prepaid and state that explicitly on the order.
- Restricted products cannot be shipped to certain countries.
- Military and diplomatic addresses use a separate carrier route and may take longer.

## Standard rule

- Carrier damaged electronics should use the damaged item process.
- Manufacturer warranty support may apply after the BrightCart return window.

# Standard Return Window

## Purpose and scope

This policy defines the default period in which customers can request a return. It should be checked before product specific restrictions such as electronics or final sale rules.

## Standard rule

The standard return window is 30 calendar days from the carrier confirmed delivery date. The request must be opened by the end of day on day 30. Shipping time back to the warehouse does not need to fit inside the 30 day window.

## Conditions and decision points

- Use the actual delivery date when available.
- If a package was never delivered, handle it as a delivery problem rather than a late return.
- A return request is considered opened when a case or self service return authorization is created.

## Worked example

An order delivered on April 2 can have a standard return request opened through May 2. If the customer ships the package on May 4 using the approved label, the request is still timely because it was opened within the window.

## Exceptions and edge cases

- Electronics have a separate 14 day rule.
- Holiday extensions may be announced in a dated seasonal notice.
- Warranty claims are not limited by the normal return window.

## Operational notes

Agents should record the delivery date and the date the return was requested

Refund Status and Failed Refunds
# Refund Status and Failed Refunds

## Purpose and scope

This runbook explains the refund lifecycle visible to support and the action to take when a refund fails. It is intended for customer support and payment operations.

## Standard rule

Refunds move through pending, issued, or failed status. A failed refund is retried automatically one time. If the retry also fails, the case must be sent to payment operations for manual review. Support must not create a second independent refund.

## Conditions and decision points

- Pending means BrightCart has accepted the request but the processor has not confirmed it.
- Issued means the processor accepted the refund.
- Failed means the processor rejected the request or the refund could not be completed.

## Worked example

A refund fails because the card account is closed. The platform retries once and receives the same failure. The support agent opens a payment operations case with the order ID and refund reference instead of pressing refund again.

## Exceptions and edge cases

- Processor outages can leave a refund pending longer than usual without marking it failed.
- Fraud holds are reviewed by risk and should not be bypassed by support.

# Webhook Delivery and Verification

## Purpose and scope

This reference explains how BrightCart signs webhook requests and how failed deliveries are retried.

## Standard rule

BrightCart signs webhook requests with HMAC SHA 256 using the integration webhook secret. Receivers must verify the signature before processing the event. Failed deliveries are retried after approximately 1, 5, 15, and 60 minutes before the event is marked undelivered.

## Conditions and decision points

- Verification should use the raw request body.
- The endpoint should return a successful 2xx response only after accepting the event.
- Consumers should handle duplicate delivery safely.

## Worked example

A webhook endpoint times out on the first delivery. BrightCart retries about one minute later. The receiver verifies the HMAC signature and uses the event ID to avoid processing the same business event twice.

## Exceptions and edge cases

- A permanently disabled endpoint stops receiving new events after it is disabled.
- Manual replay can be available for recent events.
- Network delays can shift retry timing slightly.

Keep webhook secrets out of logs and rotate them if exposed. Store

API Rate Limits
# API Rate Limits

## Purpose and scope

This article defines the default request limit for BrightCart API clients and the expected client behavior when the limit is exceeded.

## Standard rule

The default public API limit is 600 requests per minute per client. When the limit is exceeded, the API returns HTTP 429 and includes a Retry After value. Clients should wait for the indicated period and use backoff instead of immediately retrying in a tight loop.

## Conditions and decision points

- The limit is measured per registered client.
- Short traffic bursts can consume the available window quickly.
- Repeated 429 responses can indicate a design problem in polling or retry logic.

## Worked example

An integration sends more than 600 requests within the active minute and receives 429 responses with Retry After: 20. The client waits at least 20 seconds and resumes gradually rather than sending the failed requests all at once.

## Exceptions and edge cases

- Some contracted integrations can have a different approved limit.
- Webhook delivery does not consume the client's inbound API quota.
- A 503 service unavailable response is not a rate limit response.

## Operational notes

Record rate limit headers in client telemetry.

This article explains how API clients can safely retry payment and refund write operations without accidentally creating duplicate side effects.

## Standard rule

Clients should send an Idempotency Key header on supported POST payment and refund requests. BrightCart remembers the result for 24 hours. Repeating the same request with the same key during that period returns the original operation result instead of creating a second payment or refund.

## Conditions and decision points

- The key should be unique for one intended business operation.
- A retry of the same operation must reuse the same key.
- Using the same key for different request bodies can return a conflict error.

A client submits a refund and the network connection drops before the response arrives. The client retries the same refund with the same idempotency key. BrightCart returns the earlier refund result instead of issuing a second refund.

## Exceptions and edge cases

- GET requests do not need idempotency keys.
- A key older than 24 hours is outside the retention window.

Customer Data Export
# Customer Data Export

## Purpose and scope

This policy describes the self service export a verified customer can request for a copy of common BrightCart account data.

## Standard rule

A verified customer data export is normally prepared within 24 hours. When the export is ready, BrightCart sends a download link that remains valid for 48 hours. The link requires the customer to sign in again before download.

## Conditions and decision points

- The request must come from the authenticated account.
- Only data tied to the requesting account is included.
- Large accounts can take longer and will show a pending status.

## Worked example

A customer requests an export at 3:00 PM Tuesday. The file is prepared Wednesday morning and the customer receives a link. If the link is not used within 48 hours, a new export request is required.

## Exceptions and edge cases

- Data under legal restriction can be excluded or delayed.
- Payment processor data controlled by another company is not exported as raw card data.
- Business organization exports can require administrator approval.

## Operational notes

Support can explain the status but should not download the file on behalf of the customer. Expired links should be replaced by a new request, not manually reactivated.

## Purpose and scope

This policy describes multi factor authentication options and the accounts that must use MFA. It applies to customer accounts and internal administrative access.

## Standard rule

Customers may enable MFA using an authenticator app or SMS. Internal administrator accounts must use MFA and cannot disable it. Recovery codes are generated when authenticator based MFA is enabled and should be stored by the user in a safe place.

- Recovery codes are single use.

# Business ACH Payments

## Purpose and scope

This policy covers ACH bank transfer payments available to approved business accounts. Consumer accounts do not see this payment method at checkout.

## Standard rule

Approved business customers can pay by ACH. ACH payments normally take 2 to 3 business days to clear. Orders that require cleared funds are not released until the payment reaches cleared status.

## Conditions and decision points

- The business account must be approved for ACH.
- The bank account must pass verification.
- Returned ACH payments place the account on payment review.

## Worked example

A business submits an ACH payment on Monday. With no bank holiday, the payment will normally clear between Wednesday and Thursday. An order configured to wait for funds will remain on hold until the clear event arrives.

## Exceptions and edge cases

- Same day wire transfers are handled manually by finance and are not ACH.
- Weekends and bank holidays can extend clearing time.
- Very large transfers may require additional finance approval.

## Operational notes

Support can report pending or cleared status but should not promise a precise bank settlement hour. Returned payments should be escalated to finance.

- Manual replay can be available for recent events.
- Network delays can shift retry timing slightly.

# Backordered Items

## Purpose and scope

This article explains how BrightCart handles items that were orderable but are temporarily unavailable at the warehouse.

## Standard rule

A backordered item is not captured on a standard card until it ships. The order page shows an estimated availability date. If the estimate changes, BrightCart updates the order and sends a notice when the change is significant.

## Conditions and decision points

- In stock items on the same order can ship separately.
- The card must remain valid when the backordered item becomes ready.
- Customers can cancel an unshipped backordered line.

## Worked example

A customer orders two items, one in stock and one backordered. The in stock item ships and is charged first. The backordered item remains open and is captured only when it later ships.

## Exceptions and edge cases

- Gift card value can be reserved differently from a credit card capture.
- Supplier cancellation can cause BrightCart to cancel and refund the line.

API Rate Limits
# API Rate Limits

## Purpose and scope

This article defines the default request limit for BrightCart API clients and the expected client behavior when the limit is exceeded.

## Standard rule

The default public API limit is 600 requests per minute per client. When the limit is exceeded, the API returns HTTP 429 and includes a Retry After value. Clients should wait for the indicated period and use backoff instead of immediately retrying in a tight loop.

## Conditions and decision points

- The limit is measured per registered client.
- Short traffic bursts can consume the available window quickly.
- Repeated 429 responses can indicate a design problem in polling or retry logic.

## Worked example

An integration sends more than 600 requests within the active minute and receives 429 responses with Retry After: 20. The client waits at least 20 seconds and resumes gradually rather than sending the failed requests all at once.

## Exceptions and edge cases

- Some contracted integrations can have a different approved limit.
- Webhook delivery does not consume the client's inbound API quota.
- A 503 service unavailable response is not a rate limit response.

## Operational notes

Record rate limit headers in client telemetry.

Common API Error Codes
# Common API Error Codes

## Purpose and scope

This quick reference lists common HTTP responses returned by the BrightCart API and the general action expected from clients.

## Standard rule

Use 400 for malformed requests, 401 for missing or invalid authentication, 403 for authenticated clients without permission, 404 for missing resources, 409 for state conflicts, 422 for valid syntax with invalid business data, 429 for rate limits, 500 for unexpected server errors, and 503 for temporary service unavailability.

## Conditions and decision points

- Clients should read the structured error body when present.
- 4xx errors usually require a request or permission change before retrying.
- 5xx errors can be retried with bounded backoff when the operation is safe to retry.

## Worked example

A client submits a refund for an order that is already fully refunded. The API can return 409 because the requested operation conflicts with the current resource state. Retrying the identical request without changing anything will not fix the conflict.

## Exceptions and edge cases

- A gateway can return additional infrastructure errors.
- Authentication failures should not be retried indefinitely.
- A 429 should follow the Retry After

## Purpose and scope

This reference describes the BrightCart Plus subscription options used by support and checkout. It does not list temporary promotional pricing.

# Creating a Customer Account

## Purpose and scope

This guide describes the minimum information required for a BrightCart customer account. It is used by support when customers cannot finish registration.

## Standard rule

A customer account requires a unique email address, a password that meets the current password policy, and a verified phone number. One email address can be associated with only one active consumer account.

## Exceptions and edge cases

- Business organizations can have multiple users under one company profile while each user still has a unique email.
- Guest checkout does not automatically create a full account.
- Support cannot bypass phone verification for convenience.

## Operational notes

When registration fails, identify whether the problem is email duplication, password validation, phone verification, or a risk block before recommending a fix.

# Card Payment Authorization and Capture

## Purpose and scope

BrightCart authorizes the card when the order is placed and normally captures the charge when the order ships. The authorization reserves funds but is not the final settled charge. If the order is canceled before capture, BrightCart releases the authorization request.

- Some digital goods can capture immediately.

This policy defines the narrow cases in which a recently renewed BrightCart Plus subscription can be refunded. It should be used separately from the cancellation process.

## Standard rule

An annual plan renews at 9:00 AM Monday. The customer contacts support Tuesday morning and has not used any member benefit since renewal. The renewal meets the standard refund conditions.

- Fraud claims use the payment dispute process.
- Promotional credits are not refunded as cash.

# Canceling a Subscription

## Purpose and scope

This policy explains what happens when a customer cancels BrightCart Plus. Cancellation stops future renewal but does not automatically reverse a charge that already occurred.

A cancellation takes effect at the end of the current paid billing period. The customer keeps subscription benefits until that date and the plan does not renew. Cancellation by itself does not create a refund for the current period.

- A fraud related subscription charge follows the payment dispute process.

# Webhook Delivery and Verification

## Purpose and scope

This reference explains how BrightCart signs webhook requests and how failed deliveries are retried.

## Standard rule

BrightCart signs webhook requests with HMAC SHA 256 using the integration webhook secret. Receivers must verify the signature before processing the event. Failed deliveries are retried after approximately 1, 5, 15, and 60 minutes before the event is marked undelivered.

## Conditions and decision points

- Verification should use the raw request body.
- The endpoint should return a successful 2xx response only after accepting the event.
- Consumers should handle duplicate delivery safely.

## Worked example

A webhook endpoint times out on the first delivery. BrightCart retries about one minute later. The receiver verifies the HMAC signature and uses the event ID to avoid processing the same business event twice.

## Exceptions and edge cases

- A permanently disabled endpoint stops receiving new events after it is disabled.
- Manual replay can be available for recent events.
- Network delays can shift retry timing slightly.

## Operational notes

Keep webhook secrets out of logs and rotate them if exposed. Store

`redact()` replaces two kinds of placeholder test data:

1. **Fake secrets:** Any match of `FAKE_SECRET_[A-Z0-9_]+` is replaced with `[REDACTED_SECRET]`.
2. **Fake emails:** Any match of `FAKE_[^\s]+@example\.test` is replaced with `[REDACTED_EMAIL]`.

A customer account requires a unique email address, a password that meets the current password policy, and a verified phone number. One email address can be associated with only one active consumer account.

This article explains how API clients can safely retry payment and refund write operations without accidentally creating duplicate side effects.

## Standard rule

Clients should send an Idempotency Key header on supported POST payment and refund requests. BrightCart remembers the result for 24 hours. Repeating the same request with the same key during that period returns the original operation result instead of creating a second payment or refund.

# Business ACH Payments

## Purpose and scope

This policy covers ACH bank transfer payments available to approved business accounts. Consumer accounts do not see this payment method at checkout.

## Standard rule

Approved business customers can pay by ACH. ACH payments normally take 2 to 3 business days to clear. Orders that require cleared funds are not released until the payment reaches cleared status.

## Conditions and decision points

- The business account must be approved for ACH.
- The bank account must pass verification.
- Returned ACH payments place the account on payment review.

## Worked example

A business submits an ACH payment on Monday. With no bank holiday, the payment will normally clear between Wednesday and Thursday. An order configured to wait for funds will remain on hold until the clear event arrives.

## Exceptions and edge cases

- Same day wire transfers are handled manually by finance and are not ACH.
- Weekends and bank holidays can extend clearing time.
- Very large transfers may require additional finance approval.

## Operational notes

Support can report pending or cleared status but should not promise a precise bank settlement hour. Returned payments should be escalated to finance.

This policy describes multi factor authentication options and the accounts that must use MFA. It applies to customer accounts and internal administrative access.

Customers may enable MFA using an authenticator app or SMS. Internal administrator accounts must use MFA and cannot disable it. Recovery codes are generated when authenticator based MFA is enabled and should be stored by the user in a safe place.

- A verification challenge is required on new or high risk sign ins when MFA is active.
- Recovery codes are single use.

- SMS availability depends on supported phone regions.
- Support cannot read or recover an authenticator secret.

If a customer loses all second factor methods, use the account recovery process. Do not disable MFA solely based on information available to an unverified chat user.
